info.name: FIXORA — Smart Local Services Marketplace
info.description:
REST collection for the FIXORA backend.

Base URL goes through the Nginx proxy: {{baseUrl}} = http://localhost:3000/api (the backend is also reachable directly at http://localhost:8080/api).

AUTH: FIXORA has NO real authentication (no Spring Security / JWT). Protected endpoints read the X-User-Id header. The collection applies this header automatically via API-key auth:
  * default  -> {{authUserId}} (customer@fixora.local, id 2)
  * Admin/*  -> {{adminUserId}} (admin@fixora.local, id 1)
  * Provider-only requests -> {{providerUserId}} (provider@fixora.local, id 3)

Run "Auth / Login (customer)" and "Auth / Login (admin)" first: their test scripts capture the real ids into the collection variables, so the seeded ids are only fallbacks.

Seeded logins: admin@fixora.local / Admin@123  •  customer@fixora.local / Customer@123  •  provider@fixora.local / Provider@123

exec: // Nothing global to prepare; per-request scripts capture created ids.

request.description: GET /api/health — used by the Docker healthcheck and the frontend footer. Reports status and database.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Local development login/registration. No token is issued; capture the user id instead.

request.description: POST /api/auth/login. The test script stores `response.user.id` in {{authUserId}}.
POST /api/auth/login as the seeded admin. The test script stores the id in {{adminUserId}}.
POST /api/auth/login as the seeded provider. The test script stores the id in {{providerUserId}}.

request.description: POST /api/auth/register. Returns 201. ADMIN can never be self-registered. Re-running with the same email returns 409.

exec: pm.test('201 Created or 409 already exists', () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: AI
item.description: AI endpoints. Every one works without an API key: the deterministic engine answers and reports mode = fallback.

request.description: GET /api/ai/status — which provider is active, whether a key is configured, catalogue sizes.
POST /api/ai/chat — natural-language assistant grounded in the real catalogue.
POST /api/ai/search — parses intent and returns real matching services.
POST /api/ai/recommendations — rule-based scoring over real data (no invented prices).
POST /api/ai/booking-assistance — explains a service's real packages and helps pick one.

request.description: POST /api/ai/generate-service-description — drafts description copy for an admin to review/edit.
POST /api/ai/classify-complaint — suggests a category and priority for admins. A human makes the final call.
GET /api/categories — all active categories with service counts.

item.name: Catalogue — Services
item.description: Public service search, detail, packages and ratings.

request.description: GET /api/services — optional filters: categoryId, keyword, minPrice, maxPrice, city, page, size, sort.
GET /api/services/{id}/packages. Captures the first package id in {{packageId}} for booking.
GET /api/services/{id}/rating — aggregates recomputed from real review rows.
GET /api/providers — approved only. Captures the first provider id in {{providerId}}.
GET /api/providers/search — optional: city, area, keyword, serviceId.

item.name: Providers — My account
item.description: Provider dashboard. These use the provider identity (X-User-Id = {{providerUserId}}).

request.description: POST /api/bookings — price is computed server-side from the package; there is no price field. Captures {{bookingId}}.
GET /api/bookings/{id} — visible to the owning customer, the assigned provider or an admin.
PUT /api/bookings/{id}/cancel — optional body with a reason note.
POST /api/reviews — only for the caller's own COMPLETED booking. Rating aggregates are recomputed from real rows.

exec: pm.test('201 Created or 400/409 for a non-completed booking', () => pm.expect([201, 400, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: POST /api/complaints — returns 201. `category` is optional; the AI may suggest one. Captures {{complaintId}}.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: In-app only. No email/SMS/push provider is configured.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Admin-only surface. X-User-Id is forced to {{adminUserId}}; a non-admin id returns 403.

request.description: GET /api/admin/whoami — echoes the resolved admin id; handy for debugging the header flow.
GET /api/admin/dashboard — counts and recent activity from real rows.
